teacherObjectives: Critique whether an equation matches the angle diagram.
Solve angle-equation relationships and explain in words and other representations.
Write equations of forms px+q=r and p(x+q)=r for actual angle diagrams.

studentTaskComparisons.sourceDetail: Three angles on one side of a straight line are a, 90°, and b; decide whether values a and b are uniquely determined and justify.
studentTaskComparisons.currentCandidate: Existing Rich V2 fourth example already identifies underdetermination with two solution pairs. New first-party Panel A supplies a correctly labeled independent geometric analogue, not the publisher image.

studentTaskComparisons.sourceDetail: Five visually presented problems ask students to critique different proposed equations. Types include vertically opposite, supplementary, complementary, paired unknown sectors and nested angle relationships.
studentTaskComparisons.currentCandidate: New Panel B illustrates three equal sectors (x+10)° plus 30° filling a straight angle. Students must reject the distractor 3x+10+30=180; not claimed to reproduce the five original diagrams.

studentTaskComparisons.sourceDetail: Use marked intersecting, straight, perpendicular and partitioned angles to obtain unknown measures, showing organized steps. Includes multiple nested angles and an optional three-square exact-angle conjecture.
studentTaskComparisons.currentCandidate: Existing Rich V2 candidate has three numerical examples (including 3x+30=180) plus an underdetermination task. New SVG adds geometry verification and grouped px+q interpretation. Optional challenge and all source figures not demonstrated.

source.licensingRestriction: No publisher image tracing, no copied original tasks or assessment cards.

learnerTask: Without measuring the schematic in A, explain why a+b=90 gives no unique pair; draw two distinct labeled valid constructions. For B, independently partition a straight angle into three equal (x+10)° sectors and a 30° remainder, write 3(x+10)+30=180, solve x=40 and check every constructed sector. Critique the incorrect 3x+10+30 equation. Then compare a peer's different chosen equation and explain the corresponding geometry in writing.

rubricDraft.criterion: Construct two genuinely distinct valid angle diagrams for a+90+b=180 and explain why a and b are not individually determined
Draw a 180° straight angle split into three equal sectors and a 30° sector with correctly labeled rays and measures
Select, solve and check 3(x+10)+30=180; explain why the alternate 3x+10+30 form is wrong
Explain and critique peers' angle-equation choices and communicate valid geometric reasoning, not merely a numeric result

teacherAssessment.scoringDecision: Human teacher only; no automatic numeric grade or passing academic sign-off.
